title: Block Sizes for Topping Up Included Miles on a Long Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
The block in which included miles are granted to a Keyturn Trip Booking widens on long reserved periods, and widens further where a good deal of allowance has already been granted to the reservation.

| Length of the reserved period | Included miles already granted to the reservation | The block |
|---|---|---|
| 60 days or more | 3000 miles or more | 900 miles |
| 60 days or more | Fewer than 3000 miles | 750 miles |
| Fewer than 60 days | Any | The standard one |

The days of the reserved period are counted from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted. Sixty days is the figure the band turns on and it is reached, not passed: a reserved period of exactly 60 days sits in one of the first two rows, and one of 59 days sits in the third.

The included miles already granted to the reservation are the total of every grant of included miles standing on its mileage record, whatever those miles were granted for. Three thousand miles is likewise reached rather than passed: exactly 3000 miles already granted gives a block of 900 miles.

### Hypothetical readings

*A reserved period of 92 days to which 3400 included miles have already been granted.* Both limbs of the first row hold: the block is 900 miles.

*A reserved period of 92 days to which 1800 included miles have already been granted.* The reserved period is long enough but the miles granted fall short of 3000, so the block is 750 miles.

*A reserved period of 45 days to which 3400 included miles have already been granted.* The reserved period is under 60 days, so neither of the first two rows holds however many miles have been granted, and the block is the standard one.
